# Curve Preview

**Figma:** Chart/Curve-Preview 15663:110887  
**Import:** `import { CurvePreview } from "@zen-ds/react";`

A picture of a motion curve: how a value moves from its start (bottom left) to its target (the dashed line) over time, left to right — a spring, a bounce or an easing curve.

## Use it for
- Above the motion settings it previews in a property panel (Type, Duration, Bounce), so people see the effect of a change at once.
- Comparing easing choices side by side in documentation or a settings page.

## Use something else for
- Data over time → LineChart.
- A progress value → Progress.
- Choosing the curve itself → Segmented or SelectField next to the preview; the preview is not a control.

## Figma → React
| Figma | Prop | Values / notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Type | `type` | spring (default, about 4% overshoot) · bounce (visible overshoot) · ease-out (Motion/Ease/Emphasized) · ease-in-out (.65 0 .35 1) |
| Bounce | `bounce` | 0–1, how far a spring overshoots (damping ratio = 1 − bounce); default 0.3 for spring, 0.7 for bounce; ease curves ignore it |
| Name | `aria-label` | default "Motion curve: <type>" in the provider's language |

## Props
Generated from the TypeScript source; full JSON in `docs/api/curve-preview.json`.

### CurvePreview
Figma Chart/Curve-Preview (15663:110887): how a motion curve moves a value from its start (bottom left) to its target (the dashed line) over time, left to right. Place it above the motion settings it previews (Type, Duration, Bounce) so a change shows at once; it is a picture of the setting, not a control. The surface is the Input field's (Input/Background/Default, Input/Border/Default, Effect/Input, Corner-Radius/Input/Medium) so it sits with fields; grid lines Border/Neutral/Pale (as the charts), target dashed 4 · 4 Border/Neutral/Subtle, the curve 2px Content/Neutral/Strongest with round caps. For data over time use LineChart; for a progress value, Progress.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `"spring" \| "bounce" \| "ease-out" \| "ease-in-out"` | `"spring"` | The curve (Figma `Type`): `spring` (light damping, about 4% overshoot, default), `bounce` (visible overshoot), `ease-out` (Motion/Ease/Emphasized) or `ease-in-out` (.65 0 .35 1). |
| `bounce` | `number` | — | How much a spring overshoots, 0–1 (damping ratio = 1 − bounce): follow the Bounce setting the preview sits above. Default: 0.3 for `spring`, 0.7 for `bounce`. Ease curves ignore it. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | — | Name for assistive technology. Default: "Motion curve: Spring" (the type, in the provider's language). |
| `className` | `string` | — |  |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` | — |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` | — | The preview's root `<div>`. |

## ✅ Do
- Put it right above the settings it previews and pass the same values (type, bounce), so the curve follows every change.
- Let it take the panel's width: the height stays 176 and the curve stretches with the width.
- Name it after the setting when the type alone is not enough ("Back photo transition: Spring, bounce 0.3").

## ❌ Don't
- Don't use it as a chart of data; it has no axes or values to read.
- Don't pass a bounce outside 0–1 or a bounce to an ease curve (harness: curve-preview/bounce-range).

## Accessibility
- One image (role=img) named by the curve type; it is not focusable and has no keyboard of its own.
- The settings next to it carry the values; the preview only repeats them as a picture.

## Content
- Type names as the settings show them: Spring, Bounce, Ease out, Ease in and out.

## Harness (`npm run usage:check`)
| Rule | Severity | Checks | Suppress with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `curve-preview/bounce-range` | error | A CurvePreview's bounce is 0–1 and only shapes the spring curves (spring, bounce): ease curves ignore it, so the preview would not follow the setting. | `zen-allow-curve-bounce: <reason>` |
| `interaction/no-noop-handler` | warn | Every interaction a Zen control offers works: no no-op handlers (`() => {}`, `() => undefined`), which leave a field that ignores typing and ↑/↓ or a Dismiss that stays. Chat has chat/no-locked-interaction. | `zen-allow-noop-handler: <reason>` |
